headline: Connor Hellebuyck to make New Jersey Devils debut, play for first time post-trade
take:
The Athletic reports that Connor Hellebuyck is set to play his first game for the Devils after arriving over the weekend in a blockbuster trade from the Winnipeg Jets. Jesse Granger of The Athletic later posted that New Jersey beat Vegas 5-2 and that Hellebuyck "improves to 2-0-0 as a Devil."

Two games is a tiny sample, but the early signs are good. Hellebuyck has a .923 save percentage and has saved 0.5 goals above expected so far this season, meaning he has stopped slightly more than the quality of shots he faced would predict. Last season he saved 3.43 goals above expected over 57 games. The bigger story is what he steps into. NJD controls 58.4 percent of expected goals (a measure of chance quality), yet its goalies sit at minus 5.4 goals saved above expected, so the team has been outplaying opponents and getting let down in net. WPG moves the other way: 45 percent of expected goals, but its goaltending is plus 2.7. If Hellebuyck lands near his usual level, we'd expect NJD's 9-5-0 record to look sturdier.
